successors.name: Sokoto Caliphate
successors.text: the Gobir kingdom round Alkalawa on the Gulbin Rima, the Sokoto country

capitals.name: Gobir court after leaving the Aïr (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1150: the Gobirawa found a state in the Aïr.
early 15th century: the Aïr passes to the Tuareg Sultanate of Agadez.

c. 1405: the Gobir country shifts south to the Maradi region as the Aïr is lost. Region by the capital named in the infobox (Birnin Lalle from 1450); the page gives no outline or conquest, and its text has the move to Birnin Lalle in the early 18th century. [Fix af-03-x 2026-10-19: moved from 1450 to 1405 (confidence…
1450: the capital moves from Asben to Birnin Lalle (infobox "Birnin Lalle (1450-1600)"); the text has the move "in the early 18th century".

c. 1756: Babari destroys Birnin Zamfara and founds Alkalawa. "After Birnin Zamfara was destroyed (about 1756, or 1762 by other sources), Babari then established a new capital on the banks of the Gulbin Rima River."
c. 1756: the capital moves to Alkalawa (infobox "Alkalawa (1756-1808)").
3 October 1808 and after: the Gobir court falls back on the north-east.
3 October 1808: the Sultanate of Gobir ends with the fall of Alkalawa; "The state was then partially absorbed into Sokoto".

wars.name: Gobir and the jihad of Usman dan Fodio
wars.outcome: Yunfa exiled dan Fodio from Degel in 1803; the jihad began on 21 February 1804 with some initial Gobir successes (Tsuntua); Alkalawa fell on 3 October 1808 and Yunfa was killed.

wars.name: Gobir expansion and raids
wars.outcome: Around 1715 Gobir aided Zamfara's revolt against Kebbi; in the mid-18th century Soba attacked Katsina, besieged Zarma for three years, raided Gurma and Ilorin; Babari raided Katsina, Kano and Katagum.

certainty.note: No frontier on the page; the capital moved six times and the state was a mobile core with raided neighbours.
